```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(knitr)
})

kOutputDir <- file.path("..", "output", "omip51")

ReadOutput <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path(kOutputDir, name)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop(
      "The analysis output is missing: ", path, "\n",
      "Run scripts/15_omip51_bcell_dc.R first. ",
      "See the section 'Data and code availability'."
    )
  }
  read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE)
}

OutputImage <- function(name) {
  file.path(kOutputDir, name)
}

counts <- ReadOutput("gate_counts.csv")
verdicts <- ReadOutput("claim_verdicts.csv")
```

## Introduction

Liechti and Roederer published OMIP-051, a 28 colour panel for B cells,
dendritic cells and monocytes in cryopreserved peripheral blood mononuclear
cells [1]. Twelve of its markers define B cell subsets and seven define monocyte
and dendritic cell subsets. The panel resolves transitional, naive, marginal
zone and memory B cells, plasmablasts, plasmacytoid and myeloid dendritic cells,
and three subsets of myeloid dendritic cells.

The deposit FR-FCM-ZYN4 holds one PBMC file of 2,126,989 events and 59
compensation controls, 27 single stains on beads, 27 on cells, two unstained
bead controls, one unstained cell control and a stained and unstained pair for
the viability dye. It carries no analysis workspace and no fluorescence minus
one control.

This report resolves the panel to its detectors, computes the spillover matrix
from the single stains, gates the hierarchy of Figure 1, and reports each claim
the paper makes that one file can be asked to test.

## Methods

### The dataset

FR-FCM-ZYN4 was acquired on an X50-E LSRFortessa on 8 May 2018. The sample file
carries 32 parameters, of which 28 are fluorescence detectors. The compensation
controls carry between 20,000 and 300,000 events each.

Two detectors carry a marker name that lists two antibodies. `B780-A` is written
`CD27 or IgD BB790` and `R730-A` is written `IgD Ax700 or CD27 APC-R700`, so a
match on the antibody resolves CD27 to two channels and IgD to two channels.
Every marker is therefore resolved by its fluorochrome, with the antibody token
as the fallback, and the longest fluorochrome name wins so that `PE-Cy5` does
not resolve a `PE-Cy5.5` detector.

### Preprocessing

The spillover matrix is computed from the deposited single stains with
`flowStats::spillover_ng`, summarising each stained population by its median
rather than its mode. Each control is gated on its own detector first, and a
control whose gate leaves fewer than 500 events is left out and named. The
controls are matched to their detectors by the same fluorochrome rule as the
panel.

Fluorescence is transformed with an inverse hyperbolic sine at a cofactor of
150.

### Gating

The hierarchy follows Figure 1A, 1B and 1G of the paper. Events outside the
digitiser range are removed, doublets are removed on the line of forward scatter
height against area, and a robust bivariate centre on forward and side scatter
selects the cell cloud. That gate keeps the monocytes, unlike the lymphocyte
gate used elsewhere in this repository, because the next step separates them.

Every threshold below that point is placed at the 99.9th percentile of the
deposit's unstained cell control. A fitted density minimum and a two component
mixture are computed at each gate and recorded beside the threshold without
being used.

The paper places its lymphocyte gate after the B cell gate rather than before
it, to remove a high scatter population that falls inside the B cell gate. That
order is kept here so the size of that population can be counted.

### Clustering

Clustering is run as a second route to the same subsets, because it reads every
marker at once and needs no threshold. The B cells are clustered on CD10, CD20,
CD27, IgD, IgM, IgG, IgA, CD21 and CD85j, and the dendritic cell parent on CD19,
CD20, HLA-DR, CD123, CD11c, CD1c, CD141 and CD16.

Each population is sampled to 50,000 events, clustered with FlowSOM on a 10 by
10 grid into 12 metaclusters for the B cells and 10 for the myeloid cells, and
embedded with UMAP on the same channels. Every cluster is labelled by scoring
its median expression against a table of population definitions, and the margin
over the runner up is reported, because a small margin means the label is a
close call. Every step takes a fixed seed.

### Statistics

Spillover is measured by the correlation between marker pairs, on 100,000
sampled events inside the singlet gate. Two detectors that carry spillover move
together whatever the biology says, so the median absolute correlation over
every pair measures how much spillover remains without needing a gate or a
threshold.

### Software

The analysis uses flowCore, flowStats, robustbase and ggplot2. Every version is
pinned in the container.

## Results

### Channel resolution

```{r}
#| label: channels

kable(
  ReadOutput("channel_resolution.csv"),
  caption = "Every marker of the gate hierarchy, and the detector it resolves to.",
  col.names = c("Marker", "Detector", "Panel entry", "Matched by")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: ambiguous

kable(
  ReadOutput("ambiguous_markers.csv"),
  caption = "The two detectors whose marker name lists two antibodies.",
  col.names = c("Detector", "Panel entry")
)
```

All 18 markers of the hierarchy resolve by fluorochrome. The two ambiguous
detectors resolve to CD27 on `R730-A` and IgD on `B780-A`, which matches Table 2
of the paper, the names of the control files, and the name of the sample file
itself, `PBMC 22718_IgD BB790`.

### The compensation state of the deposited file

```{r}
#| label: compensation-state

kable(
  ReadOutput("compensation_state.csv"),
  digits = 4,
  caption = "The compensation keywords of the PBMC file.",
  col.names = c("File", "APPLY COMPENSATION", "Matrix size",
                "Largest off diagonal", "State")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: correlations

kable(
  ReadOutput("marker_correlation.csv"),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Correlation between markers inside the singlet gate, on 100,000 sampled events.",
  col.names = c("Compensation", "Median absolute r", "Pairs above 0.5", "Pairs",
                "CD19 with CD14", "CD20 with CD19", "IgD with CD27")
)
```

The file carries `APPLY COMPENSATION` set to TRUE beside a 28 by 28 matrix whose
largest off diagonal value is zero. The events show that the values still carry
their spillover. As deposited the median absolute correlation over the 153
marker pairs is 0.752. Applying the matrix computed from the cell controls takes
it to 0.287.

CD19 and CD20 mark the same cells. Before compensation they correlate at 0.608
and after it at 0.764, which is the direction a co-expressed pair should move.
CD19 and CD14 mark different cells, and that pair moves from 0.262 to -0.526.

### The spillover matrix from the single stains

```{r}
#| label: gateability

gateable <- ReadOutput("control_gateability.csv")
usable <- aggregate(gateable ~ control_set, data = gateable,
                    FUN = function(x) c(usable = sum(x), total = length(x)))
kable(
  data.frame(control_set = usable$control_set,
             usable = usable$gateable[, "usable"],
             total = usable$gateable[, "total"]),
  caption = "How many controls of each set could be gated on their own detector.",
  col.names = c("Control set", "Usable", "Total")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: dropped

kable(
  gateable[!gateable$gateable,
           c("control_set", "stain", "channel", "gated_events")],
  caption = "Every control that could not be gated, with the events its gate returned.",
  col.names = c("Control set", "Stain", "Detector", "Events after the gate")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: spillover-heatmap
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "The spillover matrix computed from the cell single stains. The diagonal is dropped, because it is 1 everywhere and would set the colour scale."

knitr::include_graphics(OutputImage("spillover_heatmap.svg"))
```

```{r}
#| label: agreement

kable(
  ReadOutput("spillover_agreement.csv"),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "The two matrices compared on the detectors they share.",
  col.names = c("Shared detectors", "Correlation", "Cells only", "Beads only")
)
```

The bead controls yield 27 usable stains of 27 and the cell controls 25 of 28.
The three that fail are CD141, CD16 and IgM, whose gates return 86, 13 and 145
events. The two matrices agree at a correlation of 0.870 on the 24 detectors
they share. The cell matrix is applied here, because it covers the viability
detector and the beads carry no control for it.

### The gate hierarchy

```{r}
#| label: gate-counts

kable(
  counts[, c("population", "parent", "events", "percent_of_parent")],
  digits = 2,
  caption = "The gate hierarchy of Figure 1.",
  col.names = c("Population", "Parent", "Events", "Percent of parent")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: gate-tree
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "The hierarchy, with the events and the percentage of the parent at each node."

knitr::include_graphics(OutputImage("gate_tree.svg"))
```

```{r}
#| label: gating-flow
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "The gating flow, one panel per boundary, drawn as Figure 1A of the paper draws it. Each panel shows at most 40,000 events, shaded by the local density of events so that a population inside the dense core stays visible. The vertical or horizontal line is the threshold that was applied."

knitr::include_graphics(OutputImage("gating_flow.png"))
```

```{r}
#| label: gate-cuts

kable(
  ReadOutput("gate_cuts.csv")[, c("label", "marker", "cut",
                                  "percent_above_cut", "density_cut",
                                  "percent_above_density_cut", "mixture_cut",
                                  "percent_above_mixture_cut",
                                  "parent_events")],
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Every threshold, on the arcsinh scale, beside the two fitted rules that were computed and not used. The percentage after each cut is the fraction of the parent that the cut would call positive, which is what separates a rule that works from one that fails.",
  col.names = c("Gate", "Marker", "Threshold used", "Percent above",
                "Density cut", "Percent above", "Mixture cut", "Percent above",
                "Parent events")
)
```

Monocytes are 8.17 percent of the viable events. Inside the CD14 negative cells,
29.04 percent carry HLA-DR or CD20, and 57.55 percent of those are B cells.
Within the dendritic cell parent, 13.42 percent are plasmacytoid and 23.80
percent are myeloid.

The threshold column and the density column disagree on two gates. On the
viability channel the fitted minimum lands at -1.296 and keeps 13.4 percent of
the cell cloud, where the unstained control keeps 97.35 percent. On CD14 the
fitted minimum lands at -1.956 and calls 83.4 percent of the viable events
positive, where the mixture fit gives 8.4 percent and the unstained control
gives 8.2 percent. Two independent references agreeing to within 0.2 points is
what puts the threshold where it is.

### The population inside the B cell gate that is not a B cell

The paper places its lymphocyte gate after the B cell gate rather than before
it, and states why.

> In some cases, an unusual population of SSC-AhighFSC-Ahigh cells can be
> identified within CD19+CD20+/- B cells. These cells show similar FSC-A/SSC-A
> characteristics to monocytes and were, therefore, excluded from the down-stream
> analysis of B cells by applying a lymphocyte gate after gating B cells.

Keeping that order makes the population countable. It holds 12.77 percent of the
events inside the B cell gate of this file.

### B cell subsets

```{r}
#| label: b-subsets

subsets <- counts[counts$parent %in% c("b_lymphocytes", "mature_b"), ]
kable(
  subsets[, c("population", "parent", "events", "percent_of_parent")],
  digits = 2,
  caption = "The subsets of Figure 1C, cut on the thresholds from the unstained control.",
  col.names = c("Population", "Parent", "Events", "Percent of parent")
)
```

Marginal zone B cells are 18.59 percent of B cells. Naive cells are 43.46
percent of mature B cells, IgD positive CD27 positive cells 48.59 percent and
IgD negative cells 7.95 percent. The plasmablast gate holds no events.

Transitional B cells come to 20.51 percent of B cells. That is far above the few
percent the literature reports, and it is the clearest sign of what an unstained
control cannot do. It carries none of the spillover that the other 27 dyes put
into a channel, so every threshold it sets is lower than a fluorescence minus
one control would set, and every positive fraction is therefore an upper bound.

### One dimensional cuts inside the B cell and dendritic cell gates

```{r}
#| label: one-dimensional

kable(
  ReadOutput("one_dimensional_cuts.csv"),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "A fitted cut on each marker of the lower hierarchy, and the share of the parent it selects.",
  col.names = c("Marker", "Detector", "Cut", "Rule", "Percent selected",
                "Parent")
)
```

A fitted cut selects 99.87 percent of B cells on IgM, 96.92 percent on CD85j and
87.40 percent on IgD. Inside the myeloid dendritic cells it selects 84.40
percent on CD141 and 62.66 percent on CD1c, for three subsets that the paper
separates on those two markers. These are the same markers whose thresholds the
unstained control has to supply, and neither reference resolves the three
myeloid dendritic cell subsets on this file.

### Clustering, a second route

```{r}
#| label: umap-b
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "A UMAP of 50,000 events from the CD19 CD20 gate, coloured by the label that each FlowSOM metacluster took from the definitions table. The embedding never saw the labels."

knitr::include_graphics(OutputImage("umap_b_cells.png"))
```

```{r}
#| label: b-annotation

kable(
  ReadOutput("bcell_cluster_annotation.csv")[, c("cluster", "events",
                                                 "percent_of_total",
                                                 "cell_type", "runner_up",
                                                 "margin")],
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Every B cell metacluster, the definition it best matched, and the margin over the runner up.",
  col.names = c("Cluster", "Events", "Percent", "Population", "Runner up",
                "Margin")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: umap-myeloid
#| column: page
#| fig-cap: "The same route on the HLA-DR positive CD19 CD20 negative gate. The B cell labels in this panel are the events that the CD19 and CD20 thresholds let through."

knitr::include_graphics(OutputImage("umap_myeloid.png"))
```

```{r}
#| label: myeloid-annotation

kable(
  ReadOutput("myeloid_cluster_annotation.csv")[, c("cluster", "events",
                                                   "percent_of_total",
                                                   "cell_type", "runner_up",
                                                   "margin")],
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Every myeloid metacluster, the definition it best matched, and the margin over the runner up.",
  col.names = c("Cluster", "Events", "Percent", "Population", "Runner up",
                "Margin")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: route-comparison

kable(
  ReadOutput("route_comparison.csv"),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "The two routes on the populations that carry a name in both, each as a percentage of its own parent.",
  col.names = c("Population", "Gate population", "Clustering percent",
                "Gate percent")
)
```

The two routes disagree, and the clustering sits closer to the published
expectation on every population where the two can be compared. Transitional B
cells are 4.04 percent by clustering against 20.51 percent by threshold, and the
literature places them at a few percent. Naive B cells are 67.58 percent against
43.46 percent, and they are the largest B cell subset in blood.

The plasmablast gate holds no events. The clustering labels one metacluster of
137 events as plasmablasts, on the combination of low CD20 with the highest CD27
that defines them. A threshold on CD20 inside the IgD negative cells could not
find that population, and reading nine markers at once did.

The myeloid clustering labels all three of the subsets that CD1c and CD141
define, where a fitted cut on either marker selects most of the parent. It also
labels one metacluster of 20,759 events as B cells, which is 41.52 percent of
the dendritic cell parent. Those are B cells that the CD19 and CD20 thresholds
left behind, and they are the same upper bound showing up from the other side.

Six of the ten myeloid metaclusters take the CD141 positive label, which totals
more than that subset holds in blood. The margins there run from 0.02 to 0.12,
which is what a close call looks like in this table.

## Discussion

### Principal findings

Two deposits from this laboratory carry an identity spillover matrix beside
`APPLY COMPENSATION` set to TRUE, and in both the events still carry their
spillover. On this file the median absolute correlation over 153 marker pairs is
0.752 before compensation and 0.287 after it. The keyword is not evidence about
the data, and the correlation between marker pairs settles it without a gate or
a threshold.

A marker name that lists two antibodies breaks a name match in both directions.
Resolving `IgD BB790` by its antibody sent that control to the APC-R700
detector, which transposes two rows of the matrix. The result passed no check
and looked plausible until CD19 and CD20, which mark the same cells, came out
anticorrelated at -0.700. The fluorochrome resolves both the panel and the
controls, and it is the part of the name that the deposit never leaves
ambiguous.

One threshold rule beats a rule that chooses per marker. The fitted density
minimum fails on two of the seven gates here, and it fails silently by returning
a number: 83.4 percent of viable events called CD14 positive. The deposit's
unstained cell control gives one threshold for every channel, and on CD14 it
lands within 0.2 percentage points of an independent mixture fit.

The paper's ordering of the lymphocyte gate is worth keeping. Placed after the B
cell gate rather than before it, it makes the contaminating population countable
at 12.77 percent of that gate rather than removing it unseen.

Clustering recovers what the thresholds miss. It finds a plasmablast cluster of
137 events where the gate finds none, it labels all three myeloid dendritic cell
subsets where a fitted cut on CD1c or CD141 selects most of the parent, and it
puts transitional B cells at 4.04 percent against the threshold's 20.51 percent.
Nine markers read together carry information that nine markers read one at a
time do not.

### Limitations of the thresholds

An unstained control is not a fluorescence minus one control. It carries none of
the spillover that the other 27 dyes put into a channel, so it sets every
threshold too low and every positive fraction it produces is an upper bound.
Transitional B cells at 20.51 percent of B cells, against the few percent the
literature reports, is the size of that effect on a dim marker.

The clustering shows the size of that effect from a second direction. It labels
41.52 percent of the dendritic cell parent as B cells, which are B cells the
CD19 and CD20 thresholds let through, and it cuts transitional B cells by a
factor of five. Where the two routes disagree, the threshold is the one reading
high.

Clustering is not free of the same problem. Six of its ten myeloid metaclusters
take the CD141 positive label, which is more than that subset holds in blood,
and the margins there run from 0.02 to 0.12. A label with a margin that small is
a close call rather than an answer, and the table says which ones they are.

### Limitations of the deposit

The deposit holds one PBMC file from one donor. Nothing here separates a
difference between donors from a difference between experiments, and the paper
draws every panel of its Figure 1 from the same single individual.

Three cell controls could not be gated, so the matrix applied here is built from
25 of the 28 stains. Two of the three, CD141 and CD16, are markers the myeloid
dendritic cell subsets depend on.

The plasmablast gate holds no events, and the clustering finds 137. Plasmablasts
are a fraction of a percent of B cells at steady state, and the gate that should
find them rests on a CD20 threshold from the same unstained control, inside a
parent of 12,649 events. One cluster of 137 events out of 50,000 sampled is a
small number to build a conclusion on, and this report does not build one on it
beyond saying the population is there.

## Data and code availability

```bash
# Pull the accession, about 2.0 GB of the 103 GB archive
./sync.sh pull datasets/flowrepository/OMIP-51

# Build the container. Every package version is pinned and asserted at build time.
./containers/build.sh

# The analysis
podman run --rm -v "$PWD:/work:z" -w /work everything-flow-cytometry:latest \
  Rscript scripts/15_omip51_bcell_dc.R

# This report
podman run --rm -v "$PWD:/work:z" -w /work everything-flow-cytometry:latest \
  quarto render reports/omip51_bcell_dc.qmd
```

The claims live in `gating/omip51_paper_claims.csv`, each with the sentence it
came from. The panel and its fluorochromes are in `R/omip51.R`, and the helpers
that any deposit in this repository can use are in `R/panels.R`.

```{r}
#| label: session-info

sessionInfo()
```
